commit_summary: MPC reference alignment — e_lat uses lookahead GT reference
issue: MPC optimized at-car closest-point cross-track while scoring measured lookahead-based lateral_error. On curves these diverge by P50=0.413m, causing MPC to oscillate against a misaligned reference.
deduction_eliminated: Mixed track +17.6 pts (79→96.6). Curve oscillation penalty eliminated. Lateral RMSE deduction reduced on all MPC-active tracks.
root_cause: MPC e_lat input used gt_cross_track (closest-point at car) instead of gt_cross_track_lookahead_m (PP-style reference used by scoring). On curves these references diverge — MPC corrected toward a different target than what was being scored.
process_sub: signal routing — at-car vs lookahead reference frame mismatch
prevention: Contract test: assert correlation(mpc_e_lat, -lateral_error) > 0.95 on any curve segment. Would have caught the -0.71 correlation immediately.
detection_method: mpc_pipeline_analysis correlation diagnostic showed mpc_e_lat vs lateral_error correlation = -0.71 on curves

commit_summary: Lateral accel budget regime selector replaces 6 proxy params
issue: MPC↔PP regime decisions used 6 proxy parameters (speed threshold, curvature guard, per-track mpc_min_speed_mps overrides). These proxies approximated whether MPC could track safely but failed at boundary cases where speed and curvature interact (e.g., braking into tight curves drops v² as κ rises).
deduction_eliminated: Mixed +15.3 pts (79→94.3). Eliminated 3 per-track overlay workarounds. Sloop +0.4 pts.
root_cause: Speed threshold and curvature guard were independent proxies for tire-grip feasibility. κ×v² is the actual physics quantity — a single threshold (1.5 m/s²) replaces both with correct interaction. Per-track overrides were band-aids for the proxy failures.
process_sub: proxy approximation — independent speed/curvature thresholds instead of unified physics budget
prevention: Start from physics model (lateral accel = κ×v²) when designing regime boundaries. Require dimensional analysis review for any multi-variable threshold.
detection_method: Counterfactual analysis: mixed_radius R40 corner had actual κ=0.017 (not 0.025 from geometry) because MPC tracks wider arc. Budget correctly kept MPC active.

commit_summary: Phase-gated map FF — suppress straight FF, boost entry FF
issue: Preview-curvature FF was always active on looped tracks (preview κ always visible). On STRAIGHT segments between curves, constant FF fought the centering correction, causing steering jerk. Control layer scored 80 on s_loop.
deduction_eliminated: S_loop control layer 80→100 (+20 pts). Overall s_loop 93.7→96.6.
root_cause: Map preview FF used a global gain with no phase awareness. On looped tracks the preview curvature is always nonzero (next curve visible), so FF drove steering even on straight segments where centering should dominate.
process_sub: missing state machine — continuous FF on discrete driving phases
prevention: Phase-gate all feedforward terms by default. FF should only be active in the driving phase where it adds value (ENTRY/SUSTAIN), not globally.
detection_method: Steering jerk trace showed periodic FF/centering oscillation on straight segments. Disabling map FF on straights eliminated the jerk.

commit_summary: Regime blend asymmetry fix + Stanley speed threshold
issue: When transitioning FROM Stanley/MPC back TO Pure Pursuit, no blend was applied — PP as the base controller had no transition smoothing. This caused a 46.3 steering jerk spike on sloop at the Stanley→PP handoff. Also Stanley was active at 5.0 m/s during curve braking dips, causing wider tracking.
deduction_eliminated: Sloop +3.6 pts (94.3→97.9). Mixed +15.6 pts (79→94.6). Steering jerk deduction eliminated at regime transitions.
root_cause: Blend logic only smoothed transitions TO higher-authority controllers. Return-to-PP path had no _last_regime_steering tracking, so PP steering jumped instantly. Stanley active at 5 m/s meant it engaged during curve-entry braking, widening the tracking arc.
process_sub: asymmetric transition handling — blend logic missing for return-to-base path
prevention: Test all regime transition directions (A→B AND B→A) for steering discontinuity. Regression test: max |Δsteering| at any regime transition < threshold.
detection_method: Steering jerk trace showed 46.3 spike at frame ~145 coinciding with Stanley→PP handoff

commit_summary: Inter-frame control extrapolation — decouple MPC from camera rate
issue: Camera pipeline delivers at 7.5 Hz (132ms gaps). Smith predictor delay overshoots 4× (266ms vs designed 66ms). MPC corrections reinforce error 80% of the time, causing growing oscillation Q1=0.007m → Q4=0.408m RMSE over 100s.
deduction_eliminated: Highway straight+MPC RMSE 0.146→0.025m. Oscillation growth slope 0.0047→0.0013 m/s (72% reduction). Score to 97.3.
root_cause: MPC designed for 30+ Hz updates but camera only delivers at 7.5 Hz. Smith predictor assumed 66ms delay but actual delay was 266ms (4×), creating positive feedback. No intermediate updates between camera frames.
process_sub: temporal coupling — control rate coupled to perception rate
prevention: Design control and perception as independent rate domains from the start. Assert control update rate >= minimum Hz in acceptance tests.
detection_method: analyze_oscillation_root_cause.py showed quartile-over-quartile RMSE growth with 0.18 Hz oscillation frequency matching the Smith predictor overshoot cycle

commit_summary: LMPC oscillation fix — dual-mechanism rate + gain reduction
issue: LMPC oscillated at speeds >= 14 m/s. Bicycle model gain v/L increases linearly with speed while MPC r_steer_rate was fixed — at 14 m/s the loop gain crossed the stability boundary.
deduction_eliminated: Highway straight+MPC P50 oscillation eliminated (0.003m). Highway 97.5, autobahn 96.4.
root_cause: r_steer_rate was a fixed constant but the plant gain (v/L in bicycle model) grows linearly with speed. At 14 m/s the open-loop gain crossed unity → instability. Needed speed-scheduled damping.
process_sub: missing physics model — fixed damping on speed-varying plant gain
prevention: Stability analysis: compute gain margin vs speed for any fixed-parameter MPC. Flag when plant gain variation exceeds 2× across operating envelope.
detection_method: analyze_oscillation_root_cause.py showed amplitude growth correlated with speed. Root cause confirmed by computing v/L gain crossover.

commit_summary: Bridge frame-drop regression — targetFPS 13→15 + persistent executor
issue: All hill_highway recordings had 2-4 false teleport-guard fires per run, forcing MPC→PP reset at high speed and causing artifact-driven lateral oscillation. Three A/B tests measured artifact behavior, not real dynamics — all invalid.
deduction_eliminated: Hill highway score recovered from artifact-corrupted runs. Eliminated false teleport-guard fires (forced_pp_transition_count: 0).
root_cause: Two compounding bugs: (1) targetFPS changed 15→13 which doesn't divide cleanly into Unity 60Hz physics tick, producing occasional 2-frame gaps. (2) Per-frame ThreadPoolExecutor context manager added 20-80ms variable latency. Combined gap exceeded 2.0m teleport threshold.
process_sub: timing regression — FPS change + per-frame thread pool creation
prevention: CI gate: assert forced_pp_transition_count == 0 on every recording. Assert frame interval P95 < 2× expected interval.
detection_method: teleport_jump_m HDF5 field showed jumps near 2.0m threshold. Bisection to commit 08eda7f identified the FPS change.

commit_summary: Proportional curve anticipation — local_gate_weight replacing EMA state gates
issue: Curve anticipation used binary EMA state gates (ON/OFF) on a continuous curvature signal. Transitions were all-or-nothing — either full anticipation or none — causing late turn-in on gradual curve entries and over-anticipation on exits.
deduction_eliminated: C1 late turn-in Trajectory deduction reduced. Smoother curve entry steering profile.
root_cause: Binary state gates discretized a continuous signal. local_gate_weight provides proportional response that scales with actual curvature magnitude, eliminating the threshold-crossing discontinuity.
process_sub: state discretization — binary gates on continuous signal
prevention: Design review: any time a continuous signal is gated by a binary threshold, require justification for why proportional scaling was rejected.
detection_method: Curve phase decomposition showed entry transients dominated by gate activation delay, not controller tracking error

commit_summary: Physics-based PP floor formula replacing speed table
issue: PP lookahead floor used a hand-tuned speed table mapping speed to minimum lookahead distance. The table was a proxy for the actual physics constraint (tire grip, turning radius).
deduction_eliminated: Lookahead floor now adapts correctly across full speed range. Eliminates need for per-track table tuning.
root_cause: Speed table was a discrete proxy for the continuous physics relationship between speed, curvature, and minimum safe lookahead. Table entries only covered tested speeds; interpolation between points was linear but the physics is nonlinear.
process_sub: proxy approximation — speed proxy for curvature
prevention: When a parameter depends on vehicle dynamics, derive the formula from physics first. Use tables only as overrides for empirical corrections.
detection_method: Trace tool showed floor rescue activating at wrong speeds — physics formula derived and validated immediately

commit_summary: Time-based entry term — speed-adaptive arm replacing distance threshold
issue: Curve entry anticipation used a fixed distance threshold to arm the entry term. At different speeds, the same distance corresponds to very different time-to-curve values, making anticipation too early at low speed and too late at high speed.
deduction_eliminated: Entry timing now consistent across speed range. Reduced C1 late turn-in at higher speeds.
root_cause: Distance threshold was a proxy for time-to-curve. At 6 m/s, 30m = 5s of anticipation (too early); at 12 m/s, 30m = 2.5s (about right). Speed-adaptive arm converts distance to time, giving consistent anticipation window.
process_sub: fixed threshold — distance proxy for time
prevention: For any distance-based threshold in a speed-varying system, require time-domain analysis. If the behavior should be time-invariant, use time directly.
detection_method: Per-speed-band analysis showed entry term activating 5s early at low speed but only 2.5s at high speed

commit_summary: Far preview isolation — term_time leak fix
issue: term_time (time-based entry anticipation) was computed using far preview curvature but leaked into the global steering path, affecting non-entry segments. This caused subtle steering bias on straight segments following curve exits.
deduction_eliminated: Eliminated spurious steering bias on post-curve straights. Reduced control jerk at curve exit.
root_cause: term_time was computed and added to the steering command globally. It should have been isolated to the entry phase only, gated by the same phase state machine that controls other anticipation terms.
process_sub: signal routing — term_time leaked to global path
prevention: Each steering term should have explicit phase gating. Code review: verify that any new steering term is only active in its intended driving phase.
detection_method: Steering decomposition trace showed nonzero term_time contribution on straight segments where it should be zero

commit_summary: feat: pre-computed velocity profile (fc78ad8) + activate with tracking budget (c93f800)
issue: Reactive speed planning collapsed spatial curvature into single scalar — could not reason about curve sequences, braking distances, or distinguish near vs far curves. Caused premature deceleration on hairpin straights (frame 332 cascade) and required ~29 heuristic tuning params.
deduction_eliminated: Architecture foundation — no direct scoring change at 0.05g (profile is not yet the binding constraint). Eliminates structural cause of hairpin preview saturation. Validated 7/7 tracks with 0 e-stops, 0 OOL.
root_cause: Speed planning architecture used per-frame scalar reductions (curvature_preview_abs → max() → anticipation_score → distance_weight → speed target), losing all spatial structure. Industry standard is forward+backward velocity profile over full reference path.
process_sub: design/proxy-approximation
prevention: Architecture review against industry standard (Waymo/Apollo velocity profiling) before building reactive chain. Physics-first design rule: if the quantity is a spatial function, don't collapse it to a scalar.
detection_method: Architecture analysis — hairpin failure cascade traced to scalar collapse of spatial curvature function. Calibration data (3298 curve frames) used to derive a_lat_tracking_budget_g=0.05.

commit_summary: Revert mpc_q_lat base 2.0→1.0 — undocumented tuning bundled in 41148f3 caused highway_65 59.0 regression
issue: Undocumented 2× doubling of MPC lateral weight (mpc_q_lat base 1.0→2.0) was bundled into commit 41148f3 (named 'κv² safety fade') and mirrored in 6dbdacc's _MPC_WEIGHT_AUTO_DERIVE_PARAMS. Caused MPC oversteer (command/actual 4.7×) and oscillation runaway (0.008→1.114m) on mild highway curves. Commit explicitly said 'E2E validation DEFERRED'; only unit tests run before merge.
deduction_eliminated: +82.5 points total across 4 tracks: highway_65 +40.5 (59.0→99.5), hill_highway +38.6 (59.0→97.6), s_loop +2.3, mixed_radius +1.1
root_cause: Feature commit 41148f3 bundled an unrelated 2-line tuning change (mpc_q_lat base 1.0→2.0, max cap 4.0→2.5) with the κv² safety fade feature. The commit message did not mention the tuning change, had a misleading inline comment 'base=2.0 validated' (only unit-test validated), and explicitly deferred E2E validation. No gate prevented the merge.
process_sub: testing/missing-coverage
prevention: Add a pre-merge rule: any diff touching _MPC_WEIGHT_AUTO_DERIVE_PARAMS or config/av_stack_config.yaml tuning keys requires an E2E validation record (minimum 60s run on highway_65 + one curve-heavy track). Also consider a pre-commit hook that detects numeric constant changes in tuning files and requires explicit --e2e-validated flag in the commit message.
detection_method: /iterate skill — bisect via /e2e at intermediate commits (3 runs), then git diff inspection revealed bundled q_lat change; scope-creep guard 8e caught attempted revert as too large, forcing targeted tuning-only fix

commit_summary: Reject implausible GT lane boundaries in OOL detection (hairpin_15 79.0→95.8)
issue: tools/drive_summary_core.py OOL mask trusted Unity GT boundaries blindly. At track-wrap mesh seams, gt_left/gt_right can jump to ±1500m garbage values. The analyzer counted these as real sustained OOL events (error value 1842m), inflating Safety penalty and triggering critical_yellow_layer cap. An existing 'track-end note' at analyze_drive_overall.py:2550-2563 printed a cosmetic warning but did NOT exclude the corrupt frames from the score.
deduction_eliminated: Hairpin_15 Safety 75 → 100 (+25), OOL events 1 → 0, cap released, overall score 79.0 → 95.8 (+16.8). Four other tracks unchanged (GT was clean in those runs). Architectural robustness: any future track with simulator mesh seams or failed-loop issues is now protected.
root_cause: Input validation missing on GT lane boundaries before safety-critical OOL computation. The analyzer trusted simulator output unconditionally. Compounded by a pre-existing 'fix' (track-end note) that only warned the human instead of filtering the data.
process_sub: tooling/missing-detection
prevention: Audit all sensor/GT inputs used in safety-scoring pipeline for plausibility filters. Pattern: any signal derived from simulator mesh geometry needs explicit range validation before entering scoring logic. Add a pre-commit or CI check that grep'ing for `~((gt_left <= 0) & (0 <= gt_right))` also shows a plausibility filter in the same function.
detection_method: PhilViz triage-report API at /api/recording/.../issues surfaced `out_of_lane: max_error: 1842.964m, source: ground_truth_boundaries` — the 1842m value is physically impossible and pointed directly at GT corruption. Also surfaced by direct HDF5 inspection showing gt_left/gt_right jump at frame 1873 of hairpin recording.

commit_summary: b532c1b fix(nightly): retro step writes instead of asking; ProcessType Interactive for Unity jobs
issue: Global Stop hook fired /retro in claude -p nightly jobs; skill step 4 ends in 'Proceed?' which no one can answer, so four nights of memory proposals exited 0 unwritten. Separately, ProcessType=Background made launchd throttle the Unity-launching agents: preflight dt_p95 360-436 ms for 17 nights vs 153 ms interactive, blocking fresh ACC data for 94 nights.
deduction_eliminated: No score change; restored fresh ACC data (28 recordings in 8 nights) and the nightly retro's memory writes (6 new indexed memories in 11 nights).
root_cause: Interactive defaults leaking into unattended contexts: an interactive confirmation gate in an unattended skill; a background QoS class on a job that must render at 30 FPS. caffeinate prevents sleep, not QoS throttling.
process_sub: tooling/unattended-contract
prevention: State non-interactive contracts in each PROMPT.md (heartbeat-invariant rule); when a launchd job underperforms the same command run by hand, check ProcessType before hardware.
detection_method: three-clocks check on preflight logs; grep of nightly logs for unwritten proposals; identical dt_p95 band across 17 nights

commit_summary: 95294ec fix(acc): no CUTOUT while a lead is detected; bypass jerk cooldown in ACC states (+ EB closing-rate threshold and gap floor)
issue: hill_g2 TTC_ESTOP every night since 2026-08-12. (1) Below cutout_speed_mps the ACC ramps its target toward free-flow and the owner-resolver hands the governor's 12 m/s to the controller with a stopped lead 7 m ahead. (2) Jerk cooldown x0.4 per frame pinned IDM's -7 m/s2 demand at -0.43 (5.9% delivered) on flat ground; bypass only fired for |gravity|>=0.1 or emergency states. (3) EMERGENCY_BRAKE re-entered on Doppler noise at standstill (124x per stop) with the EB floor 3.0 m above s0 2.0 m.
deduction_eliminated: G2 Safety 50 -> 100 (TTC_ESTOP 5/5 -> 0/5 in Unity A/B; EB entries 124 -> 0); G2 composite 72.8 -> 94.7 PASS on night 42 together with the radar-frame fix.
root_cause: State-machine hand-off and limiter interaction, not the grade: CUTOUT semantics ignore a detected lead; the cooldown scales an IDM-driven command; EB thresholds were written in a frame where they were unreachable. Three prior write-ups blamed actuator latency, grade feed-forward and IDM decel.
process_sub: design/signal-routing
prevention: Reproduce ACC failures in tests/acc_closedloop_harness.py before recording forensics; every ACC state transition needs a test with a detected lead at low speed; limiter bypass conditions must enumerate the controller that owns the command.
detection_method: tests/acc_closedloop_harness.py counterfactual sweep (13 knobs x 27-point plant grid), confirmed by run_ab_batch 5 pairs

commit_summary: 16c4bc6 fix(acc): compensate centre-to-centre radar range; count physical contact as collision
issue: radar_fwd_distance_m is |leadCenter - egoTransform|; physical contact occurs at a reported ~4.43 m, so min_gap_s0_m 2.0, EB floor 3.0, collapsed-gap 0.5 and near-miss 2.0 were all inside the lead body. The scorer counted collisions as distance<0 (unsatisfiable: override clamps to 0.1) and never read vehicle/lead_collision_detected - every hill_g2 run, hill_g1 09-04/09-07 and highway_h5 09-09 were contacts reported as 0 collisions; H5 scored PASS 100 with a 0.5 m true margin.
deduction_eliminated: G2 physical contact 5/5 -> 0/5 (Unity A/B), TTC_min 1.65 -> 2.48; scorer collision-forces-zero fires for the first time; historical G2/G1/H5 composites re-score to 0 (honesty, not regression).
root_cause: Sensor measurement frame never specified against the gap thresholds that consume it; the honest collision signal existed in the schema and had no reader; the harness's idealised radar hid the gap until a Unity A/B disagreed with it.
process_sub: requirements/measurement-frame
prevention: Record sensor frame/offset in provenance (done); recorder<->analyzer schema contract test asserting every safety signal has a reader; harness sensor models default to the measured frame, not the idealised one; scorer collision from lead_collision_detected.
detection_method: Unity A/B disagreed with harness; lead_collision_detected scan across September recordings; AVBridge.cs read

commit_summary: 561df49 fix(config): speed_drag_gain derive-table base 0.035 → 0.0 to match T-ACC-DRAG removal
issue: e3474e2 zeroed control.longitudinal.speed_drag_gain in the base config but the orchestrator's _SPEED_CONTROL_SCALING_PARAMS table still carried 0.035; tests/test_auto_derive_curvature.py::test_speed_control_params_exist_in_base_config was REAL_BREAK for two nights and the nightly agent read it as 'the removal was silently undone'. Recording snapshots show 0.0 ran — the table never overrode the explicit key.
deduction_eliminated: none (test consistency); prevented a false 'fix undone' diagnosis from steering the next ACC A/B
root_cause: Two sources of truth for one parameter (YAML base value + derive-table base) with a test enforcing equality but no lint at edit time.
process_sub: implementation/wrong-config
prevention: Derive-table entries should read their base from the loaded config instead of restating it; until then, run tests/test_auto_derive_curvature.py after any control.longitudinal / control.lateral YAML edit.
detection_method: full pytest run before commit (-x stopped on it)

commit_summary: ea2b92b feat(scoring): grade lateral error at the car, not at the lookahead reference point
issue: control/lateral_error is ref_x — the trajectory reference point's vehicle-frame offset 3.7–7.2 m ahead (= d_at_car + Ld·sin ψ + ½Ld²κ). Every lateral RMSE/P95, the 0.40 m comfort gate, out-of-lane, centered %, the apex/late-turn-in classifier and every A/B graded it. Against Unity's at-car road-frame cross-track (fiducial-verified) it over-reported gentle curves 2–5× (hill_highway 0.192 vs 0.033) and UNDER-reported tight ones (s_loop 0.116 vs 0.345, hairpin_15 0.173 vs 0.600). Months of curve tuning, the 'PP ceiling' and the CURVATURE_FLOOR_COEFF proxy were aimed at measurement geometry.
deduction_eliminated: hill_highway Trajectory penalty 30 (cap) → ~1 on the April golden; sweeping_highway Traj 92.9 → 95.4 (passes); s_loop 99.1 → 79.0 and hairpin 98.7 → 59.0 (honesty, not regression — strict xfail via GOLDEN_BELOW_FLOOR)
root_cause: The controller's convenience error signal (reference-point offset) was adopted as the product metric without a frame definition; the MPC branch corrected its own copy in April (Frenet d) but the scorer never followed. The recorder's at-car ground truth existed on every file since April and was read by nothing.
process_sub: requirements/wrong-metric
prevention: Every scored quantity names its frame and reference point in scoring_registry; any 'floor' or 'unavoidable error' constant in the scorer must cite the physics (a measurement artifact is a metric bug, not a floor). Cross-check scored error against an independent ground truth (fiducials) when registering goldens.
detection_method: A/B on pp_map_ff_wheelbase_m: steering changed 25%, in-curve error did not move at all → decomposed control/lateral_error against mpc_gt_cross_track_at_car_m and the lane-line fiducials

commit_summary: 64d08d9 fix(trajectory): seed the curvature source without hysteresis; highway ACC runs the production stack
issue: AVStack._select_primary_curvature started on lane_context and applied the 3-frame switch-on hysteresis to the FIRST selection, so frames 0-1 of every run used the perception curvature of a stationary car (0.09-0.17 1/m on a straight) while the map was already healthy. That junk seeded the 12 m distance-based curvature EMA; the speed governor turned it into comfort = 3.0 m/s and curve cap = comfort - 0.4, and a car held at 3 m/s crosses the window slowly, so launch was frozen for ~12 s. Hidden since March because acc_highway.yaml (149 inherited non-ACC keys) disabled both governor caps and curvature smoothing instead of fixing the base.
deduction_eliminated: H8 FAIL -> PASS (engage edges 23 -> 1, cone rejects 6 -> 0 %, at-car RMS 0.39 -> 0.09 m, analyzer 79 -> 96-98); H2 under the minimal overlay gap RMSE 41 -> 19 m, converges 23 -> 15 s. Highway ACC scenarios now measure the production stack (lateral 0.33-0.40 -> 0.08-0.14 m). highway_65 base track unchanged (planner ramp below the comfort cap).
root_cause: State-machine initialisation: hysteresis meant to stop source chatter was applied when there was no previous source to protect, and a stateful downstream filter (distance EMA) trusted its first sample. Compounded by a process defect: the March overlay worked around the symptom (caps off) in a scenario config rather than root-causing it in the base, which both hid the defect and made every ACC scenario run a different stack from the sweep.
process_sub: design/state-discretization
prevention: Rule: a hysteresis/debounce gate must bypass on first selection (no prior state); stateful consumers of curvature_primary_abs must ignore hysteresis_hold frames (architecture.md). Rule already in CLAUDE.md but violated in March: never fix a base behaviour in a scenario overlay; tests/test_config_overlays_respect_base_safety.py now exists and the highway overlay is minimal, so an overlay-vs-base divergence shows up as a config diff. Diagnostic that found it in minutes: print the first 12 frames of curvature_primary_source / curvature_selection_reason / speed_governor_comfort_speed / active_limiter at launch.
detection_method: Launch-profile dump of the H2 minimal-overlay A/B recordings (comfort speed decaying as a distance-EMA of a frame-0 spike), then reading _select_primary_curvature; decay physics confirmed by replaying the recorded speed trace through trajectory.utils.smooth_curvature_distance (tests/test_curvature_source_seed.py)
